books.title: Ghosts
books.author: Henrik Ibsen
books.desc: A respected widow prepares to open an orphanage in her late husband's memory, but the return of her son brings the hidden past back to life.
about: Mrs Helen Alving, the widow of a respected captain and chamberlain, is about to open an orphanage built in her husband's memory. Pastor Manders, her old friend and adviser, arrives for the ceremony, and her beloved son Oswald, a painter, has come home from Paris. As the young maid Regina and her father, the carpenter Engstrand, pursue their own plans, Mrs Alving reveals to Manders the truth about her marriage, and the past returns to haunt them all.

Ibsen's drama attacks hypocrisy, empty duty and the dead ideas and conventions that weigh on the living, the "ghosts" of the title. Its frank treatment of subjects such as hereditary disease and the failures of marriage made it one of the most controversial plays of its century.

Ghosts was published in Copenhagen in December 1881 and caused a scandal; theatres in Scandinavia refused to stage it, and its first performance took place in Chicago in 1882, in a production for Scandinavian immigrants. This edition offers the English translation by William Archer and the German translation by Marie von Borch.

books.title: An Enemy of the People
books.author: Henrik Ibsen
books.desc: A town doctor discovers that the new public baths are poisoned, but when he tries to tell the truth, the whole town turns against him.
about: Dr Thomas Stockmann is medical officer of the baths that have brought new prosperity to his small coastal town. When he discovers that the water is contaminated and endangering visitors' health, he expects to be thanked for his discovery. Instead his brother Peter, the town's mayor, the local newspaper editor Hovstad and the printer Aslaksen, speaking for the respectable majority, turn against him to protect the town's finances.

Ibsen's play is a sharp drama about truth, public interest, the press and the tyranny of the majority. Dr Stockmann, idealistic, stubborn and sometimes comic, ends by declaring that the strongest man in the world is the one who stands most alone.
An Enemy of the People was written in 1882 and first performed at the Christiania Theatre in January 1883. This English translation is by R. Farquharson Sharp.

books.title: Lady Windermere's Fan
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.desc: On her birthday, young Lady Windermere suspects her husband of an affair with the mysterious Mrs Erlynne, who has been invited to her ball.
about: Lady Windermere, young, happily married and strict in her principles, is preparing for her birthday ball when she learns from the gossiping Duchess of Berwick that her husband has been visiting a woman of doubtful reputation, Mrs Erlynne, and giving her money. To her horror, Lord Windermere insists on inviting Mrs Erlynne to the ball. Hurt and angry, Lady Windermere is tempted by the declarations of the charming Lord Darlington.

Behind the glittering epigrams of high society, Wilde's first great comedy questions the hypocrisy of moral judgements and the idea that people can be simply divided into good and bad. Its subtitle is "A Play About a Good Woman".
Lady Windermere's Fan was first performed on 20 February 1892 at the St James's Theatre in London, produced by the actor-manager George Alexander, who had encouraged Wilde to write it.

books.title: Arms and the Man
books.author: George Bernard Shaw
books.desc: During a Balkan war, a romantic young woman hides an enemy soldier who carries chocolates instead of cartridges, and her ideas about war and love collapse.
about: In 1885, during the war between Serbia and Bulgaria, Raina Petkoff, the daughter of a wealthy Bulgarian family, dreams of her fiancé Sergius, the dashing hero of a cavalry charge. That night a fugitive soldier fighting for the Serbs climbs into her bedroom: Captain Bluntschli, a practical Swiss mercenary who carries chocolates rather than ammunition. She hides him, and when the war ends he unexpectedly returns.
Shaw's comedy mocks romantic illusions about war, heroism and love, contrasting Sergius's empty gallantry with Bluntschli's common sense. Raina calls him her "chocolate cream soldier".
Arms and the Man was first performed on 21 April 1894 at the Avenue Theatre in London. This edition includes an introduction by an unnamed writer.

books.title: She Stoops to Conquer
books.author: Oliver Goldsmith
books.desc: Tricked into thinking a country house is an inn, a young man shy with ladies but bold with barmaids woos his intended bride, who plays a maid to win him.
about: Young Charles Marlow travels to the country to meet Kate Hardcastle, the bride his father has chosen for him. Marlow is painfully shy with respectable women but bold with servants and barmaids. Thanks to a joke by Kate's mischievous stepbrother, Tony Lumpkin, Marlow and his friend Hastings take the Hardcastles' house for an inn and treat her father like a landlord. Kate seizes the chance to "stoop to conquer", pretending to be a barmaid to win his heart.

Goldsmith's comedy of mistakes, disguise and good humour mocks pretension and celebrates natural feeling. Its comic characters, from the bumbling Mr Hardcastle to Tony Lumpkin, keep the action lively through one long night.

She Stoops to Conquer; or, The Mistakes of a Night was first performed at Covent Garden Theatre in London on 15 March 1773 and was a great success. Goldsmith dedicated the published play to Samuel Johnson.
